correctness_confidence.basis: Lean 4 kernel with 18 theorems (0 sorry, 0 custom axioms) and AST-audited Python exact rational solver over Q guarantee complete algebraic and numerical correctness.

novelty.basis: Independent machine-audited formalization and certificate suite auditing recent hitting time index bounds, disproofs, and quintic scaling.

reproducibility.basis: Fully reproducible via Lean 4.35.0 and Python 3.10 with automated script execution and 16 canonical JSON certificates.

rigor.basis: Strict separation of scope between decoupled N-arithmetic in Lean and exact rational linear systems in Python, complemented by 39 adversarial forgery tests.

significance.basis: Resolves key conjectures on hitting time indices, degree thresholds, and lollipop graph maximizers with rigorous machine certification.

strengths: Rigorous machine-checked Lean 4 kernel with 0 sorry and 0 custom axioms.
Zero-float exact rational verification over Q using fractions.Fraction and AST auditing.
Comprehensive canonical certificate suite (C01-C16) and 39 adversarial forgery-rejection tests.
Clean separation of scope between decoupled arithmetic/monotonicity proofs and finite-graph linear system solves.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact rational finite-witness certificate suite for hitting time index bounds and degree thresholds.
summary: The paper presents an exceptionally rigorous, machine-checked verification package (HT-INDEX-CERT-1.0) auditing hitting time index bounds, degree thresholds, and lollipop graph counterexamples from Palacios et al. (2026). It combines an 18-theorem constructive Lean 4.35.0 kernel with zero axioms/sorry and an AST-audited zero-float Python exact rational solver over Q across 16 canonical JSON certificates and 39 adversarial tests. The methodology, algebraic formulations, and cryptographic manifest reproducibility are exemplary.
weaknesses: Scope is dependent on prior theoretical results from Palacios et al. (2026), serving as an independent audit and formalization artifact rather than a standalone theoretical derivation paper.
